Mildly positive with clear downside notes: The Fed highlights strong job gains and robust household spending, but also weak business fixed investment and exports alongside inflation below 2% and low market-based inflation compensation. Given evidence that investment is interest-rate and finance sensitive—especially inventories and fixed investment being constrained by internal funds (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994)—the 25 bp cut and money-market operations should support capex and stabilize transmission. With expected inflation central to current inflation dynamics in New Keynesian models (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003), low inflation expectations justify a dovish tilt but also underscore downside risk. Overall tone: cautiously positive.

"Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low."
